newsitem.title: USA: Fixed-rate mortgage rates inch up in week.
newsitem.headline: Fixed-rate mortgage rates inch up in week.

text.p: Fixed-rate mortgage rates edged higher this week, but adjustable loans became more affordable, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.

Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 8.16 percent in the week ended Sept. 27, up from 8.14 percent last week. Fifteen-year mortgages also rose slightly to an average of 7.68 percent from 7.64 percent.
One-year adjustable mortgage rates inched lower to 5.82 percent from 5.83 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.62 percent, the 15-year 7.16 percent, and the adjustable loan 5.77 percent.
"Interest rates have largely remained in a narrow band around 8 percent since the middle of July," said Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist.
"Affordable rates have helped insure a strong housing market through August and this trend should continue into the Fall," Nothaft added.
The Federal Open Market Committee decided Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged.
On Wednesday, the National Association of Realtors said sales of U.S. August existing homes fell 0.5 percent.
Also, the Commerce Department will issue U.S. new home sales data for August on Monday.
Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, both unchanged from last week. Charges on adjustable loans were also unchanged at 1.4 percent.
Separately, the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said the volume of U.S. mortgage applications rose 5.8 percent in the week ended Sept. 20.
The volume of applications to refinance mortgages rose 5.0 percent in the latest survey week, while applications to purchase mortgages rose 6.0 percent, the trade group said.
